column2: Threat of automatic distribution of malicious code in the grid system
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of introducing and running malicious code on behalf of a trusted process on any of the grid system resource centers and its automatic distribution to all grid system nodes. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in grid computing technology – a high level of automation with low administratibility of the grid system. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has the privileges of a legal user of the grid system.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of aggregation of data transmitted in the grid system
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of disclosure of protected information by the violator by identifying the nodes involved in its processing, collecting, analyzing and summarizing data intercepted in the grid system's data transmission network. 
This threat is caused by the weakness of grid computing technology – the use of unprotected Internet channels as a transport network of the grid system. 
Implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder has: 
forces and resources sufficient to compensate for the extreme distribution of grid tasks between grid system nodes; 
privileges sufficient to intercept data network traffic between grid system elements (nodes)
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of exploiting weaknesses in cryptographic algorithms and vulnerabilities in their implementation software
column3:
The threat is the ability to identify weaknesses in cryptographic algorithms or vulnerabilities in the software that implements them. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in cryptographic algorithms, as well as errors in the program code of cryptographic tools, their interface with the system, or their configuration parameters. 
The threat can be implemented if the intruder has information about the encryption tools used in the system, the encryption algorithms implemented in them, and their settings
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of hardware reset of the BIOS password
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of resetting passwords set in the BIOS / UEFI without going through the authorization procedure in the system by de-energizing the BIOS chip (removing the battery) or installing a jumper in a regular place on the system board (switching the "jumper").
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in some system (motherboards) – the presence of hardware password reset mechanisms installed in the BIOS/UEFI. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has physical access to the computer's system unit
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of introducing malicious code in the BIOS
column3:
The threat is the ability to force the BIOS/UEFI to execute malicious code every time the computer starts up by embedding it in the BIOS / UEFI by replacing the BIOS/UEFI chip or updating the BIOS/UEFI software to a version that already contains malicious code. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the control technologies for updating the BIOS/UEFI software and replacing the BIOS/UEFI chipset. 
The implementation of this threat is possible during the repair and maintenance of the computer
column4: A high-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of code or data injection
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of impact on programs with high privileges
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Information system, virtual machine, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of recovery and / or reuse of authentication information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of accessing user data as a result of selecting (for example, by full search or dictionary search) the authentication information of the discredited user account in the system, as well as by intercepting and reusing the password hash to restore the session.
This threat is caused by the following disadvantages: 
significantly smaller amount of data for the hash code of authentication information compared to it itself (the time for selecting hash codes is less than the time for full search of authentication information); 
weaknesses in the hash code calculation algorithm that allow it to be reused for successful authentication. 
Implementation of this threat is possible with the help of special software tools, as well as in some cases – "manually"
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat to restore a previous vulnerable BIOS version
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of a process leaving the VM
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility that a malicious program can launch its own hypervisor, which functions at a level of logical interaction lower than the compromised hypervisor. 
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the hypervisor software, which implements the function of a sandboxed software environment for programs running in it, as well as weaknesses in hardware support instructions for virtualization at the processor level.
The implementation of this threat leads not only to the compromise of the hypervisor, but also to the protection tools running in the virtual environment created by it, and, consequently, to their inability to perform security functions against malicious programs that operate under the control of their own hypervisor.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Information system, network node, storage medium, file system objects, user credentials, virtual machine image

column2: Threat to deauthorize an authorized wireless network client
column3:
The threat is caused by the ability to automatically terminate the connection of a wireless access point to an authorized wireless network client.
This threat is caused by the weakness of network communication technologies over wireless data transmission channels – information about the MAC addresses of wireless clients is available to all network interaction participants. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder connects a device to the wireless network, the MAC address of which will completely coincide with the MAC address of the discredited authorized client.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of destructive changes to the program configuration/environment
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of destructive software impact on the discredited application by manipulating the configuration files or libraries used by it. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the integrity control measures of configuration files or libraries used by applications. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator has the rights to write to file objects associated with the configuration / environment of the program, or the ability to redirect requests of the discredited program from protected file objects to false ones.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: System software, Application software, network software, firmware, metadata, file system objects, registry

column2: Threat of destructive use of declared BIOS functionality
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of misuse of the declared BIOS/UEFI functionality to violate the integrity of information stored on external storage media and in the computer's random access memory. 
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the BIOS/UEFI software intended for testing and maintaining the computer (memory integrity checking tools, RAID controller management software, etc.). 
The implementation of this threat may be facilitated by the ability to update some BIOS/UEFI without passing authentication.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of long-term retention of computing resources by users
column3:
The threat consists in the ability of an intruder to restrict end-user access to a computing resource by forcibly holding it in a loaded state by repeatedly performing certain destructive actions or exploiting vulnerabilities in programs that distribute computing resources between tasks. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the load balancing and computing resource allocation mechanisms. 
A threat can be implemented if the intruder has the ability to make requests that collectively take longer to complete than the user's requests.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Information system, network node, storage medium, system software, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of access to protected files using a workaround
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of accessing local server files using URLs
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that the intruder sends a request for access to the user's file system to the discredited browser instead of a URL request. In this case, the browser executes this request with the rights it was granted at startup, and passes the data obtained as a result of this operation to the intruder. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for checking user input requests, which does not distinguish between requests for file system access and URL requests. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has privileges to send requests to the browser operating in the discredited system.
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of access/interception/modification of HTTP cookies
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access by the violator to the protected information (user accounts, certificates, etc.) contained in cookies, during their storage or transmission, in read mode (disclosure of confidentiality) or writing (making changes to implement the threat of spoofing a trusted user).
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the cookie protection measures: the lack of verification of the entered data by the network service that uses cookies, as well as the lack of encryption when transmitting cookies.
The implementation of this threat is possible under the conditions of successful unauthorized access to cookies by the violator and the lack of verification of the integrity of their values by the discredited application.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of loading an abnormal operating system
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder replacing the loaded operating system by unauthorized reconfiguration of the access path to the operating system loader in the BIOS/UEFI.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the technologies used to differentiate access to BIOS/UEFI management.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the following BIOS/UEFI configuration parameter is available to the intruder-indicating the source of loading the operating system
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of DNS cache infection
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder redirecting network traffic through its own network node by indirectly changing the correspondence tables of IP and domain names stored in the DNS server, by generating an avalanche of possible responses to a DNS server request to a legitimate user, or by exploiting DNS server vulnerabilities. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the authentication mechanisms of network interaction actors, as well as DNS server vulnerabilities that allow you to directly replace the DNS cache of the DNS server. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has sufficient privileges to send network requests to the DNS server.
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of abuse of opportunities provided to consumers of cloud services
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that a consumer of cloud services (an intruder) can send spam, unauthorized access to the virtual machines of other cloud service consumers, or perform other destructive software actions on various systems using leased cloud server resources. 
This threat is caused by the fact that the consumer of cloud services can install their own software on the cloud server. 
This threat can be implemented by installing and running malicious software on the cloud server by the consumer of cloud services. Successful implementation of this threat by a cloud service consumer has a negative impact on the reputation of the cloud service provider
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of abuse of trust of cloud service consumers
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that the security of cloud service consumers ' information may be violated (accidentally or intentionally) by internal intruders of the cloud service provider.
This threat is caused by the fact that a significant part of the security functions has been transferred to the responsibility of the cloud service provider, as well as the inability of the cloud service consumer to take protection measures against the actions of the cloud service provider's employees. 
This threat can be implemented if cloud service consumers are not part of the organization that provides these cloud services (i.e., the consumer has actually transferred their own information to the provider for processing).
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of excessive RAM allocation
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of allocating significant RAM resources to serve malware requests and, accordingly, reducing the amount of RAM resources available in the system for allocating in response to requests from legitimate users ' programs.
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in the mechanism for controlling the allocation of RAM to various programs. 
This threat can be implemented if malicious software is found in the active state of the system
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of changing components of an information (automated) system
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder gaining access to the network, files, bookmarks, etc. by unauthorized changes in the composition of the software or hardware of the information system, which in the future will allow this intruder (or another external one who has discovered an unauthorized access channel to the system) to perform unauthorized actions in this system. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in control measures for the integrity of the hardware configuration of the information system. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator successfully obtains the necessary permissions in the system and is able to connect additional peripheral equipment
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Information system, server, workstation, virtual machine, system software, application software, hardware

column2: Threat of changing the operating modes of computer hardware elements
column4: A high-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of changing system and global variables
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder's indirect destructive software impact on some programs or the system as a whole by changing the common system and global variables used by discredited programs. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the shared memory access control mechanism, as well as vulnerabilities in application software modules that control the integrity of external variables. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has successfully unauthorized access to system and global variables and there is no verification of the integrity of their values by the discredited application
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of XML schema corruption
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder changing the algorithm of information processing by applications operating on the basis of XML schemas, up to bringing the application into a "denial of service" state, by changing the XML schema transmitted between the client and the server. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to ensure the integrity of data transmitted during client-server interaction, as well as weaknesses in the network interaction mechanism of open systems.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has successfully unauthorized access to network traffic transmitted between the client and server, and the discredited application does not check the integrity of the XML schema.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of distortion of information entered and output to peripheral devices
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of misinformation of users or automatic control systems by replacing or distorting the source data coming from sensors, keyboards or other input devices, as well as replacing or distorting information output to the printer, operator's display or other peripheral devices.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in anti-virus protection measures and control over the validity of input and output data, as well as errors made during special checks of computer hardware. 
This threat can be implemented if the discredited information system contains malicious software (for example, virtual device drivers) or hardware bookmarks
column4: External intruder with high potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, hardware

column2: Threat of using alternative ways to access resources
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, file system objects, application software, system software

column2: Threat of using supercomputer computing resources by "parasitic" processes
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of a significant decrease in the performance of the computing field of the supercomputer and the efficiency of running current parallel calculations on it due to the consumption of computing resources of the supercomputer by "parasitic" processes ("descendant processes" of previous tasks or processes launched by malicious software).
This threat is caused by weaknesses in memory cleaning measures for "descendant processes" of completed tasks, as well as processes started by malicious software. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the completed tasks are completed incorrectly or if malicious processes are present in the supercomputer's memory in the active state
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of using default identification/authentication information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for the violator to pass the authorization procedure based on identification and authentication information obtained from open SOURCES_X000D_
or from the information service corresponding to the "default" account of the discredited security object. 
This threat is caused by the fact that many software and hardware manufacturers provide "default" accounts intended for initial login to the system, or by the fact that when passing the registration procedure on the information service, the automatic password generation mechanism issues the same or similar passwords to users with similar logins. Moreover, on many devices, 
identification and authentication information can be returned to the "default" setting after performing a hardware reset of system parameters (the Reset function). 
The implementation of this threat is possible under one of the following conditions:
 the violator has information about the manufacturer/model of the security object and the availability in open sources of information about identification and authentication information corresponding to the "default" account for the security object;  the
violator successfully completes the procedure for identifying this information during the analysis of the program code of the discredited security object
whether the intruder has information about the login used when registering the attacked user
column4: Internal intruder with low potential; External intruder with medium potential
column5: Information protection tools, system software, network software, firmware, software and hardware with built-in protection functions

column2: Threat of using authorization mechanisms for privilege escalation
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder gaining access to data and functions intended for accounts with higher privileges than the intruder, due to errors in the configuration parameters of access control tools. At the same time, the intruder does not perform a destructive software impact on the system to increase its privileges, but only uses existing errors.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in program and file access control measures. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has any privileges in the system
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of using fake BIOS digital signatures
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of installing a vulnerable version of the BIOS/UEFI update or a version containing malicious software but digitally signed. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to control the reliability of digital signature issuing centers.
This threat can be implemented if an unreliable certificate authority issues a digital signature for a version of the BIOS/UEFI update containing vulnerabilities, or for a version containing malicious software (i.e., if such a center performs forgery), as well as if the intruder substitutes a trusted update source
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of exploiting weaknesses in input data encoding
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator of destructive information impact on the discredited system by manipulating the values of input data and the form of their provision (alternative encodings, incorrect file extension, etc.). 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the input data control mechanism. 
This threat can be implemented under the following conditions: 
the discredited system accepts input data from the intruder; 
the intruder has the ability to control one or more input data parameters
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware, Registry

column2: Threat of exploiting weaknesses in network/local data exchange protocols
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access by the violator to the protected information transmitted in the system due to the destructive impact on the network/local data exchange protocols in the system by violating the rules for using these protocols.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the protocols themselves (the algorithms embedded in them), errors made during the implementation of protocols, or vulnerabilities introduced by automated design/development tools. 
This threat can be implemented if there are weaknesses in the network/local data exchange protocols.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Network software, Network traffic

column2: Threat of using weak cryptographic BIOS algorithms
column3:
The threat lies in the complexity of verifying real operation parameters and algorithms implemented in BIOS/UEFI cryptographic tools. However, trust in cryptographic protection will be limited to trust in the BIOS manufacturer. 
This threat is caused by the complexity of using native cryptographic algorithms in the BIOS/UEFI software. 
The ability to implement this threat reduces the reliability of the assessment of the real level of security of the system
column4: External intruder with high potential

column2: Threat of research of the program's working mechanisms
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for the violator to reverse engineer the program code and further study its structure, functionality, and composition in order to determine the program's algorithm and search for vulnerabilities in it.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for protecting the program code from research. 
This threat can be implemented if:
 the intruder has access to the source files of the program;
 the intruder has access to the program distribution and there is no mechanism to protect the program code from investigation
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware

column2: Threat of app research through bug reports
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder investigating the algorithm of the discredited application and its intended structure by analyzing the error reports generated by this application. 
This threat is caused by the placement of protected information (or information that can be generalized to reveal protected information about the system) in the generated error reports. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has access to error reports generated by the application and there is redundancy in the data contained in them.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware

column2: Threat of running out of computing resources for big data storage
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of a temporary denial-of-service condition in the big data warehouse. 
This threat is caused by the constant difficult-to-control filling of occupied disk space due to data continuously coming from various information sources, and weaknesses in information access and storage technologies in big data warehouses. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the data transfer rate is instantaneous (current) exceeding the speed of their storage (due to insufficient bandwidth of the communication channel or the speed of allocating free space and saving incoming data to it) or if there is a temporary lack of free space in the storage (due to incorrect storage management or as a result of the intruder's destructive software effects on the storage filling control mechanism by changing parameters or logic of its operation)
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of running out of keys required for updating the BIOS
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of violation (impossibility of implementation) of the BIOS/UEFI update procedure when the stock of keys necessary for its implementation is exhausted.
This threat is caused by a limited set of keys required for updating the BIOS/UEFI.
The implementation of this threat is possible by exploiting vulnerabilities in the key set update tools, or by using key search software tools by the violator.
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of a conflict of jurisdictions in different countries
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of refusal to transfer protected information across borders within the framework of cloud services in accordance with the requirements of the local legislation of countries whose residents participate in the provision of cloud services. 
This threat is caused by the fact that, depending on the specifics of the legislation of various countries whose residents participate in the provision of cloud services, legal measures of various jurisdictions can be used to ensure information security. 
The implementation of this threat is possible provided that information security in the course of providing cloud services is subject to legal measures of various jurisdictions that contradict each other in a number of issues
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Cross-site Scripting Threat
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of the intruder introducing malicious code sections on the site of the discredited system in such a way that it will be executed on the workstation of the user viewing this site. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the security verification mechanism when processing requests and data coming from the website. 
The threat can be implemented if the client software supports script execution, and the intruder has the ability to send requests and data to the discredited system.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of cross-site request forgery
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that the violator sends a link to a web resource containing malicious code to the discredited user, and when they click on it, illegal malicious actions will automatically be performed on behalf of the discredited user. 
This threat is caused by browser vulnerabilities that allow you to perform actions without confirmation or authentication by a discredited user. 
The threat can be implemented if the discredited user saves authentication information using the browser.
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of cloud server availability violation
column3:
The threat is the possibility of stopping the provision of cloud services to all consumers (or a group of consumers) due to a violation of the availability of cloud infrastructure for them. 
This threat is caused by the fact that ensuring availability is not a specific requirement for information security for cloud technologies, and, in addition, cloud systems are implemented in accordance with a service-oriented approach. 
This threat can be implemented when one or more cloud servers go into a denial-of-service state. Moreover, the ability to dynamically change the volume of cloud services provided to consumers can be used by an intruder to implement a threat. At the same time, a successfully implemented threat against just one cloud service can disrupt the availability of the entire cloud system.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of breaking the isolation of user data inside the VM
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that malicious software operating outside the VM can compromise the security of user data of programs operating inside the VM.
This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in the hypervisor software, which ensures that the address space used for storing user data of programs operating inside the VM is isolated from unauthorized access by malicious software operating outside the VM.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the malicious program code successfully overcomes the boundaries of the virtual machine not only by exploiting the hypervisor's vulnerabilities, but also by performing such an impact from lower (relative to the hypervisor) levels of system functioning
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of BIOS execution environment isolation violation
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of changing the parameters and/or logic of the BIOS / UEFI software operation by software intervention from the computer's operating system or by unauthorized access to the network communication channel of the server service processor.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in technologies used to differentiate access to the BIOS / UEFI, its administration and update functions, from the operating system or communication channels. 
This threat can be implemented:
from the operating system – provided that the BIOS/UEFI functionality is available for updating and/or managing the BIOS / UEFI software from the operating system; 
from the network side – provided that the discredited server service processor has sufficient privileges to manage the entire system, including modifying the BIOS/UEFI servers of the system, and the discredited server
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of violation of the authentication procedure for subjects of virtual information interaction
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of spoofing the subject of virtual information interaction, as well as in the possibility of a state of inability to implement such interaction. 
This threat is caused by the presence of many different protocols for mutual identification and authentication of virtual, virtualized, and physical access subjects that interact with each other during data transfer both within one level of the virtual infrastructure and between its levels. 
This threat can be implemented if errors occur during authentication of subjects of virtual information interaction
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, metadata, user credentials

column2: Threat of grid system failure under atypical network load
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of a significant decrease in the performance of the grid system, up to a temporary disruption of its performance when an atypical network load appears (including those caused by a distributed DoS attack, the activity of other users on the network, etc.). 
This threat is caused by the weakness of grid computing technologies – the performance of the grid system strongly depends on the load of communication channels, which is a consequence of the maximum territorial distribution of the grid system computing module among all types of information systems.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the grid system task manager does not have sufficient control over the state of individual grid system nodes
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of violation of information processing technology by unauthorized changes to VM images
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Virtual machine image, network node, network software, virtual machine

column2: Threat of cache data integrity violation
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder placing incorrect (potentially dangerous) data in the cache of an application (for example, a browser) or a service (for example, DNS or ARP) in such a way that the discredited application (or service) will consider this data correct before updating the cache. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the cache integrity control mechanism. 
This threat can be implemented if the attacker has successfully unauthorized access to cache data and there is no verification of the integrity of data in the cache by the discredited application (or service)
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of incorrect detection of the format of input data entering the big data warehouse
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of distortion of information stored in the big data warehouse, or failure to save when transferring data in some formats to it. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in technologies for determining the format of input data based on additional service information (file headers and network packets, file extensions, etc.), as well as technologies for adaptive selection and application of methods for processing multi-format information in big data warehouses. 
This threat can be implemented if additional service information about the data does not correspond to its actual content for any reason, or the big data warehouse does not implement methods for processing data in the resulting format.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of inability to restore the PC session when switching out of intermediate power states
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of losing unsaved data processed in the previous session of work on the computer, as well as in the possibility of losing time to resume work on the computer. 
This threat is caused by errors in the implementation of computer hardware and software components related to power supply. 
This threat can be implemented if the computer cannot be brought out of intermediate power states ("standby mode", "hibernation", etc.).
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Workstation, storage media, system software, metadata, file system objects, registry

column2: Threat of not being able to migrate VM images due to hardware and software incompatibilities
column3:
The threat is caused by the possibility that the cloud service consumer will have insurmountable difficulties in changing the cloud service provider due to technical difficulties in implementing the procedure for migrating VM images from the cloud system of one cloud service provider to the system of another. 
This threat is caused by the fact that each cloud service provider uses hardware and software from various manufacturers to implement its activities, some of which may use manufacturer-specific instructions, protocols, methods, switching schemes, and other features of implementing its functionality. 
This threat can be implemented if the standard software data exchange interfaces (APIs) for implementing the procedure for migrating VM images between different cloud service providers in one or both directions are incompatible. 
This threat also restricts the ability of the cloud service provider to change hardware and software manufacturers, which may lead to a violation of the integrity and availability of information due to the fault of the cloud service provider.
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Cloud infrastructure, virtual machine, hardware, system software

column2: Threat of inability to manage user rights in the BIOS
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of unauthorized use by users of the declared BIOS/UEFI functionality aimed at administrators. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in technologies for differentiating access (distribution of rights) to the BIOS/UEFI functionality between different users and administrators. 
This threat can be implemented if you have physical access to the terminal and, if necessary, to the computer's system unit.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of unfair performance of obligations by cloud service providers
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of disclosure or damage to the integrity of the protected information of cloud service consumers by the cloud service provider, failure to meet the requirements for the quality level (availability level) of access to their programs or information systems imported into the cloud provided to cloud service consumers. 
This threat is caused by the inability of consumers to directly control the actions of cloud service provider employees.
Implementation of this threat is possible in cases of negligence on the part of employees of the cloud service provider, insufficient job descriptions and other instructions of these employees, insufficient measures for managing and ensuring the security of cloud services, etc.
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Information system, server, storage medium, metadata, file system objects

column2: Threat of unsecured cloud service administration
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of implementing indirect destructive software effects on some or all of the information systems operating in the cloud environment, by intercepting control over the cloud infrastructure through remote administration mechanisms. 
This threat is caused by insufficient attention paid to monitoring the data entered by users of cloud services (including authentication data), as well as vulnerabilities in insecure data exchange interfaces (APIs) used by remote administration tools. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder receives authentication information (when entering it in public places) from legitimate users, or exploits vulnerabilities in remote administration tools.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of poor-quality infrastructure migration to the cloud
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of reducing the real level of security of an information system that immigrates to the cloud due to errors made during migration during the transformation of its real infrastructure to the cloud. 
This threat is caused by the fact that the transformation of even a part of the information system infrastructure to the cloud often requires major changes in such infrastructure (for example, in security policies and the organization of network data exchange). 
This threat can be implemented if the software and network interfaces are incompatible or the security policies do not match when the information system is transferred to the cloud
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Information system migrated to the cloud, cloud system

column2: Threat of uncontrolled copying of data inside a big data warehouse
column3:
The threat lies in the complexity of controlling all automatically created copies of information in the big data warehouse due to temporary inconsistency of these operations.
This threat is caused by duplicating (double or multiple) data on various computing nodes that are part of the big data warehouse, in order to increase the speed of access to this data with a large number of read/write requests. However, this operation is an internal function and is "opaque" to end users and big data warehouse administrators. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if there are insufficient measures to control automatically created copies of information used in the big data warehouse.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Big data storage, metadata, protected data

column2: Threat of uncontrolled growth in the number of virtual machines
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of limiting or disrupting the availability of virtual resources for end users of cloud services by accidentally or unauthorized deliberate creation of multiple virtual machines by the intruder. 
This threat is caused by the limited amount of disk space allocated for the virtual infrastructure, and weaknesses in technologies for controlling the process of creating virtual machines. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator has rights to create virtual machines in the cloud infrastructure
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Cloud system, Cloud Infrastructure management console, cloud infrastructure

column2: Threat of uncontrolled growth in the number of reserved computing resources
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of refusing to allocate computer resources to legal users after the violator has unlawfully reserved all available computer resources (computing resources and memory resources).
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the software of the virtual infrastructure management level, which implements the function of distributing computer resources between users. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator successfully performs unauthorized access to the software of the virtual infrastructure management level, which implements the function of distributing computer resources between users.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of uncontrolled destruction of information by a big data warehouse
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of deleting some processed data from the storage without notifying the end user or administrator.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for automatic deletion of data that does not meet certain requirements (maximum" lifetime " in the repository, final inconsistency with other data, creating a copy in another location, etc.). 
This threat can be implemented if the measures implemented in the big data warehouse to control automatic data deletion are insufficient
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Big data storage, metadata, protected data

column2: Threat of incorrect setting of the transaction data structure
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of fraud committed by the violator (database client) by interrupting the transaction or spoofing the transaction ID. In the first case, the transaction is incomplete, and in the second case, the user forcibly completes the transaction, changing its ID, and notifying that the transaction was not completed, thereby provoking the transaction to be repeated. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for monitoring the continuity of transactions and the integrity of data transmitted during a transaction between the database and its client
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential

column2: Threat of incorrect use of a transparent proxy server due to browser plugins
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of redirecting or copying data processed by the browser through a transparent proxy server connected to the browser as a plugin. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the browser settings access control mechanism. 
Implementation is possible if the intruder successfully enables the transparent proxy server usage mode in the browser settings, for example, as a result of the cross-site scripting threat implementation
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of incorrect use of software and hardware functionality
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of using the declared capabilities of software and hardware in a certain (non-standard, incorrect) way in order to destructively affect the information system and the information it processes. 
This threat is related to weaknesses in the data processing mechanism and commands entered by users. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has access to software and hardware.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware, Hardware

column2: Threat of incorrect implementation of licensing policies in the cloud
column3:
The threat is the possibility that cloud service consumers may be denied remote access to the leased software (i.e., the availability of the SaaS cloud service is lost) due to the fault of the cloud service provider. 
This threat is caused by insufficient consideration of the issue of managing licensing policies for the use of software from various manufacturers in the cloud. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the software licensing policy is based on limiting the number of installations or users of the software, and the created virtual machines with licensed software are used many times.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: The threat of uncertainty in the distribution of responsibility between roles in the cloud
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of significant disagreements between the provider and the consumer of cloud services on issues related to determining their rights and obligations in terms of ensuring information security. 
This threat is caused by the lack of a sufficient set of measures to control the distribution of responsibility between different roles in terms of data ownership, access control, cloud infrastructure support, and so on. 
The ability to implement this threat increases if you use cloud services provided by other providers (i.e., if you use a scheme for providing cloud services with intermediaries).
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of uncertainty of responsibility for cloud security
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of non-compliance with a number of information protection measures by both the cloud service provider and their consumer.
This threat is caused by the lack of a clear division of responsibility in terms of ensuring information security between the consumer and the cloud service provider. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if there is insufficient documentation of the division of responsibilities between the parties involved in the provision of cloud services, as well as the lack of a documented definition of responsibility for non-compliance with security requirements.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to protected information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized accidental or deliberate familiarization of the user with information that is not intended for him, and its further use to achieve their own or other persons (organizations) ' s destructive goals.
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in access control tools, errors in the configuration parameters of these tools, or the absence of the specified tools. 
The implementation of this threat does not imply the installation and use of special malicious software by the violator. At the same time, familiarization can be carried out by viewing information from other users ' monitor screens, from printed documents, by eavesdropping on conversations, etc.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Hardware, storage media, file system objects

column2: Threat of illegal or incorrect use of the app interaction interface
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing a destructive program impact on the API in order to implement functions that were not originally provided for by the discredited application (for example, using debugging functions from the API). 
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in the mechanism for checking input data and commands of the API used by the software. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has access to the API and the discredited application does not have a mechanism for checking input data and commands
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware, Registry

column2: Threat of illegal actions in communication channels
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder making changes to the operation of network protocols by adding or deleting data from the information flow in order to influence the operation of the discredited system or gain access to confidential information transmitted over the communication channel. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network protocols, which consist in the lack of verification of the integrity and authenticity of the received data. 
Implementation of this threat is possible if the violator performs unauthorized access to network traffic
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of continuous modernization of cloud infrastructure
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of introducing vulnerabilities and weaknesses to the cloud system along with adding new software or hardware. At the same time, a system considered protected at the stage of its commissioning can no longer be considered as such after its modernization. 
This threat is caused by the fact that, firstly, cloud service providers provide an opportunity for the consumer of cloud services to choose and / or change the initial composition of the cloud infrastructure software in the process of providing such services, and, secondly, when new consumers are actively connected, the cloud infrastructure may be upgraded several times a year. 
Implementation of this threat is possible if the period until the next upgrade does not exceed the period for evaluating the system's compliance with security requirements in the absence of a cloud service management system and ensuring their security (cloud management systems).
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized recovery of deleted protected information
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized shutdown or bypass of the BIOS write protection mechanism
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of introducing malicious program code into the BIOS/UEFI after the user mistakenly or maliciously turns off the BIOS / UEFI write protection mechanism, as well as in the possibility of installing an unsigned update that bypasses the BIOS/UEFI write protection mechanism. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to restrict access to the management of the BIOS/UEFI write protection mechanism, as well as vulnerabilities in the BIOS/UEFI update mechanism that lead to buffer overflow. 
This threat can be implemented in one of the following conditions: 
when the BIOS/UEFI write protection mechanism is turned off; 
the intruder successfully exploits a vulnerability in the BIOS/UEFI update mechanism that leads to a buffer overflow
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to active and / or passive virtual and / or physical network equipment from the physical and / or virtual network
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of malicious programs changing the algorithm of operation of the network equipment software and (or) its configuration parameters by exploiting vulnerabilities in the software and (or) firmware of the specified equipment. 
This threat is caused by limited functionality (the presence of weaknesses) active and / or passive virtual and / or physical network equipment that is part of the virtual infrastructure, if this equipment has a fixed network address. 
This threat can be implemented if there are vulnerabilities in the software and / or firmware of the network equipment.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Network hardware, firmware, network software, virtual devices

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to authentication information
column3: The threat consists in the possibility of extracting passwords, usernames, or other credentials from the computer's RAM or stealing (copying) password files (including those stored in clear text) from machine storage media
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, file system objects, user credentials, registry, machine storage media

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to virtual transmission channels
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing unauthorized interception of network node traffic that is inaccessible using network technologies other than network virtualization technologies, by incorrect use of such technologies. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the flow control, firewall, and access control measures implemented for network virtualization technologies (which are used to build virtual data channels).
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has privileges to interact using network virtualization technologies
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Network software, network traffic, virtual devices

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to the hypervisor from a VM and / or physical network
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder bringing the entire (if the hypervisor is one) or part (if several hypervisors interact with each other) of the virtual infrastructure into a "denial of service" state by performing a destructive program action on the hypervisor from virtual machines running in the virtual environment created by it, or by influencing the hypervisor through its connection to a physical network. computer network.
This threat is caused by the presence of many different interfaces of interaction between the hypervisor and the virtual machine and /or physical network, vulnerabilities of the hypervisor, as well as software vulnerabilities and limited functionality of the hardware used to ensure its operability. 
This threat can be implemented in one of the following cases:
 the intruder has sufficient privileges to perform destructive software actions from virtual machines;
 the hypervisor has an active interface for interacting with the physical computer network
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to data outside the reserved address space, including that allocated for virtual hardware
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of a malicious program operating inside a VM violating the integrity of the program code of its own and / or other virtual machines running under the same hypervisor, as well as changing its (their) configuration parameters. 
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in the hypervisor software, which ensures that the address space used for storing not only protected information and the program code of the programs that process it, but also the program code that implements virtual hardware (virtual devices for processing, storing and transmitting data) is isolated from unauthorized access by malicious programs operating inside the virtual machine.
The implementation of this threat is possible if unauthorized access by a malicious program operating inside the VM to data stored outside the address space reserved for user data of this VM is successfully performed
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Server, workstation, virtual machine, hypervisor, machine storage media, metadata

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to protected virtual machines from the virtual and / or physical network
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing a destructive software impact on virtual machines from a virtual and / or physical network, both using standard (non-virtual) network technologies and using network virtualization technologies. 
This threat is caused by the presence of network addresses for the created VMs and the possibility of their network interaction with other actors. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has information about the network address of the virtual machine, as well as the current activity of the virtual machine at the time of the intruder's destructive software impact.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to protected VMs by other VMs
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of destructive software impact on protected virtual machines from other virtual machines using various mechanisms for data exchange between virtual machines implemented by the hypervisor and activated in the system. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the data exchange mechanism between VMs and vulnerabilities in its implementation in a specific hypervisor. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has sufficient privileges to use various mechanisms for data exchange between virtual machines implemented in the hypervisor and activated in the system.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to protected virtual devices from the virtual and / or physical network
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for an intruder to remotely gain unauthorized access to virtual devices from a virtual and / or physical network using various network technologies used for data exchange in a system built using virtualization technologies. 
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in the network software interfaces of hypervisors designed for remote management of the composition and configuration of virtual devices created (created) by these hypervisors. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has sufficient privileges to exchange data in a system built using virtualization technologies.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Virtual data storage, processing, and transmission devices

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to the local computer via the grid system client
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for an intruder to perform a network login to the grid system node with the rights of one of the accounts corresponding to the software processes of the task management system, and then gain access to the private part of the cryptographic certificates used to establish communication in the grid system. 
This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in the client of the grid system (client software installed in the nodes of the grid system), the operation of which allows the intruder to perform read and write operations in objects of the local file system of the computer, send signals to program processes (including shutdown signals), read and write operations to the memory of program processes corresponding to connecting software and grid tasks, opening network connections in local and external nodes of the grid system. 
This threat can be implemented if malicious program code is introduced into the task management system. In fact, the presence in a grid system node of software unknown to its owner (the grid system client) that performs unknown calculations is a "black box" through which (by exploiting vulnerabilities or software bookmarks) an intruder can perform illegal actions in relation to the protected information stored in the grid system node (personal information of the node owner)
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to computing field segments
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access by an intruder to the source data, intermediate and final calculation results of other users of the supercomputer, as well as accidental or deliberate destructive impact of the processes of solving some problems on the processes and results of solving other computational problems. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for differentiating access of subjects to segments of computing fields of the supercomputer. 
The implementation of this threat is possible when performing tasks of different users of the supercomputer on the same computing field of the supercomputer
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to the system via wireless channels
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder gaining access to the resources of the entire discredited information system through the wireless data transmission channels used in its composition. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the identification/authentication protocols (such as WEP, WPA and WPA2, AES) used to access wireless equipment. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder has specialized software that implements the functions of exploiting vulnerabilities in wireless network identification/authentication protocols, as well as being located at the point of receiving signals from the discredited wireless network.
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, user credentials, network traffic, hardware

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to the data storage system from a virtual and / or physical network
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of performing destructive software effects on virtual data storage devices and (or) virtual disks (which are both segments of virtual disk space created by a separate virtual device, and a single virtual disk space created by logically combining several virtual data storage devices).
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in the technologies used to distribute information across various virtual storage devices and / or virtual disks, as well as weaknesses in the single virtual disk space technology. These weaknesses are related to the high complexity of algorithms for ensuring consistency of actions for distributing information within a single virtual disk space, as well as interaction with virtual and physical data transmission channels to ensure work within a single disk space.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder has special software tools that can exploit the weaknesses of the technologies used in the construction of the data storage system (network technologies, information distribution technologies, etc.).
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to protected information stored in the virtual space
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of violating the confidentiality of information contained in distributed files containing protected information by restoring the data of distributed files from their many individual fragments using software and information technologies for processing distributed information. 
This threat is caused by the fact that due to the use of a variety of virtualization technologies designed to work with data (data distribution within virtual and logical disks, data distribution between such disks, data distribution between physical and virtual drives of a single disk space, allocation of disk space areas as separate disks, etc.), almost all files are stored in a single disk. stored as a set of individual segments. 
This threat can be implemented if there are insufficient or no measures to ensure the confidentiality of information stored on individual storage devices
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized modification of authentication information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access by an intruder to the authentication information of other users using standard operating system tools or special software tools. 
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in access control measures for authentication information. 
The implementation of this threat may contribute to further penetration of the intruder into the system under the account of a discredited user.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, file system objects, user credentials, registry

column2: Threat of unauthorized use of privileged BIOS functions
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder using potentially dangerous BIOS/UEFI capabilities. 
This threat is caused by the presence of potentially dangerous functionality in the BIOS/UEFI
column4: External intruder with high potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized copying of protected information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder illegally obtaining a copy of the protected information by performing a sequence of illegal actions, including: unauthorized access to the protected information, copying the found information to removable media (or to another place accessible to the intruder outside the system). 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanisms for delineating access to protected information and controlling access of persons in the controlled area.
This threat can be implemented if there are no cryptographic security measures or a copy is removed at the time of processing the protected information in unencrypted form
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: File system objects, machine storage media

column2: Threat of unauthorized registry editing
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder making changes to the registry used by the discredited application, which affect the functioning of individual services of the application or the application as a whole. In this case, the registry is understood not only as the registry of the Microsoft Windows operating system, but also as any registry used by the application. Changing the registry can be either a stage in the implementation of other destructive actions, or the main goal. 
This threat is caused by the weaknesses of the access control mechanism, which consists in assigning too high privileges to programs that implement it when working with the registry. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator gets the rights to work with the registry editing program
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software that uses the registry, registry

column2: Threat of unauthorized user account creation
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder creating an additional user account in the system and then using it for their own illegal purposes (logging in with the rights of this account and performing destructive actions in relation to the discredited system or from the discredited system in relation to other systems).
This threat is caused by weaknesses in access control mechanisms for protected information. 
Implementation of this threat is possible if you also have the rights to run specialized programs for editing files containing information about system users (for remote access) or regular access controls from the operating system (for local access).
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized deletion of protected information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator causing economic, informational, moral and other types of damage to the owner and operator of illegally deleted information by performing destructive software or physical effects on the machine storage medium. 
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to ensure the availability of protected information in the system, as well as the presence of vulnerabilities in the software that implements these measures. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator obtains system rights to erase data or physical access to the machine storage medium at a distance sufficient to provide an effective destructive effect.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Metadata, file system objects, and registry

column2: Threat of unauthorized remote out-of-band access to hardware
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder obtaining system management privileges by using remote out-of-band (via an independent TCP/IP auxiliary channel) access. 
This threat is caused by the inability to control the mechanism that implements remote access functions at the hardware level, at the operating system level, as well as independence from the power state of hardware devices, since this mechanism provides for the procedure for remote switching on / off of hardware devices. 
This threat can be implemented
if:  the system has hardware that supports remote out-of-band access technology;
 the system is connected to public networks (the Internet)
column4: External intruder with high potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized buffer management
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access to the data contained in the clipboard by an intruder in order to get acquainted with the information stored there or to carry out destructive software effects on the system (for example, buffer overflow to execute arbitrary malicious code).
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for delimiting access to the clipboard, as well as weaknesses in the mechanisms for checking input data. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator successfully performs unauthorized access to the segment of RAM of the discredited object in which the clipboard is located.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of unauthorized synchronization and state management
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware

column2: Threat of unauthorized pointer management
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder executing arbitrary malicious code on behalf of a discredited application or putting the discredited application in a "denial of service" state by changing pointers to memory locations containing certain data used by the discredited application. 
This threat is related to vulnerabilities in the means of delimiting memory access and controlling the integrity of the contents of memory cells. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has privileges to change the pointers used by the discredited application.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of inconsistency in the security policies of cloud infrastructure elements
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder performing destructive software actions against both cloud service providers and consumers. 
This threat is caused by insufficient consideration of the issue of managing security policies for cloud infrastructure elements due to the significant distribution of the cloud infrastructure. 
This threat can be implemented if you use different security policies that are not consistent with each other (for example, one security tool may deny access and another may grant access).
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of inconsistency in big data access rules
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of providing erroneous unauthorized access to protected information or, conversely, the possibility of denying access to protected information to legal users due to errors made when delegating privileges to them by other legal users of the big data warehouse. 
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to differentiate and coordinate access to information of different users in the big data warehouse. 
This threat can be implemented if you use different security policies that are not consistent with each other (for example, one security tool may deny access and another may grant access).
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of detecting open ports and identifying network services associated with them
column3:
The threat consists in the ability of the intruder to determine the status of network ports of the discredited system (so-called port scanning) to obtain information about the possibility of establishing a connection to the discredited system using these ports, the configuration of the system itself and the installed information security tools, as well as other information that allows the intruder to determine which ports destructive software actions can be for what reasons – only using special techniques to bypass firewalls. 
This threat is related to vulnerabilities and configuration errors in the firewall and network traffic filtering tools used in the discredited system. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has a connection to the discredited computer network and specialized software that implements port scanning and network traffic analysis functions
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Host Detection Threat
column3:
The threat consists in the ability of the intruder to scan the computer network to identify working network nodes. 
This threat is related to weaknesses in network communication mechanisms that provide network clients with open technical information about network nodes, as well as vulnerabilities and configuration errors in the firewall and network traffic filtering tools used in the discredited system. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has a connection to the discredited computer network and specialized software that implements network traffic analysis functions.
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat to bypass incorrectly configured authentication mechanisms
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder obtaining privileges in the system without passing the authentication procedure by performing actions that violate the conditions for the correct operation of authentication tools (for example, entering data in an unsupported format).
This threat is caused by incorrect values of authentication tools configuration parameters and / or lack of input data control. 
This threat can be implemented if there are errors in the specified values of the authentication mechanisms configuration parameters
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat to public availability of cloud infrastructure
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access to the protected information of one cloud service consumer by another. 
This threat is caused by the fact that due to the peculiarities of cloud technologies, consumers of cloud services have to share the same cloud infrastructure. 
This threat can be implemented if errors are made when separating elements of the cloud infrastructure between consumers of cloud services, as well as when isolating their resources and separating data from each other
column4: External intruder with medium potential
column5: File system objects, hardware, and cloud server

column2: Threat of indirect management of a group of programs through shared data
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder indirectly changing the algorithm of a group of programs that use shared data at the same time, by intercepting control over one of them (RAM cells, global variables, configuration files, etc.). 
This threat is caused by the presence of weaknesses in the mechanism for monitoring changes made to the general data of each of the programs in the group. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder successfully intercepts control of one of the programs in the group of programs that use shared data
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat to defining security object types
column3:
