The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder analyzing the output data of the discredited system using a method that allows you to determine the exact values of parameters and properties that are uniquely inherent in the discredited system (this method is known as "fingerprinting", from English "fingerprinting"). The use of this method does not directly harm the discredited system. However, the information collected in this way allows the intruder to identify weaknesses in the discredited system, which can be used later in the implementation of other threats. 
This threat is caused by errors in the configuration parameters of firewall tools, as well as the lack of mechanisms for controlling input and output data. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator has information about the relationship of the output data with the configuration of the discredited system (software documentation, data transmission standards, specifications, etc.).
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat to defining a computer network topology
column3:
The threat consists in the ability of the intruder to determine the state of network nodes of the discredited system (so-called network scanning) to obtain information about the topology of the discredited computer network, which can be used later in attempts to implement other threats. 
This threat is related to weaknesses in network interaction mechanisms that provide network clients with open technical information about network nodes, as well as vulnerabilities in firewall tools (the operation algorithm and configuration of network traffic filtering rules).
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder has the ability to connect to the computer network under study and has specialized software that implements the network traffic analysis function.
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of failure to load input data in an unknown format by a big data warehouse
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility that the big data store refuses to accept input data of an unknown format from a legitimate user. 
This threat is caused by the lack of a mechanism for independent (automatic) adaptation to new data formats in the big data warehouse. 
This threat can be implemented if you receive a request to upload input data of an unknown format to the storage.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of denial of service by the supercomputer storage system
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of a significant slowdown in the terminal sessions of all users of the supercomputer, up to the point that the entire supercomputer reaches the "denial of service" state when the maximum achievable load on the parallel file system of the supercomputer is exceeded. 
This threat is caused by a significant increase in the number and volume of data stored on the drive for some computing tasks. 
The implementation of this threat is possible under the condition of intensive file I / O in the cluster file subsystem of a supercomputer based on the use of a parallel file system.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of disabling control sensors
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of providing an intruder with information isolation of the security system by interrupting the communication channel with control sensors that monitor system state parameters, or disrupting the operation of the sensors themselves. In this case, the system will stop responding to both safety incidents (if the sensors that were turned off were part of the safety system, for example, motion sensors) and other types of incidents (for example, when the fire alarm sensors are turned off, pressure increases in hydraulic units, etc.). 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in information security measures in automated process control systems, as well as the presence of vulnerabilities in the software that implements these measures. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if access (physical or software) is obtained to the communication lines of the security system with control sensors or to the sensors themselves
column4: External intruder with high potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Hypervisor update error threat
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of discrediting the security mechanisms that work on the basis of the hypervisor that prevent unauthorized access to VM images due to errors in updating it. 
This threat is caused by the dependence of the functioning of each virtual device and each virtualized access subject, as well as the entire virtual infrastructure (or part of it, if more than one hypervisor is used) on the health of the hypervisor. 
This threat can be implemented if errors occur during the hypervisor update process: 

 updates that introduce new errors in the hypervisor code;  updates
that introduce program code into the hypervisor that causes incompatibility of the hypervisor with its operating environment; 
other information security incidents
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of going through all app settings and parameters
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of an intruder gaining access to additional hidden functionality (information about which was not published by the developer) or bringing the system into a "denial of service" state when the intruder sets some program configuration parameters, reaching such parameter values by iterating through all possible combinations.
This threat is caused by software vulnerabilities that occur when it is incorrectly configured. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has privileges to change the software configuration. When implementing this threat, unlike other similar threats, the intruder acts "blindly" - simply by sorting through all possible combinations
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software, Firmware, Registry

column2: Threat of grid system overloading with computational tasks
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of reducing the throughput of resource centers when a large number of tasks are sent by one user (the intruder) accidentally or intentionally, which may make it impossible for other users of the grid system to queue tasks for execution. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the grid system's control measures over the number of computational tasks started by grid system users. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator has the rights to queue tasks for execution by the grid system
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of data transmission over hidden channels
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of transmitting prohibited commands to numerically controlled hardware
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that the violator may damage the actuators, the workpiece and /or the processing tool of the numerically controlled equipment by transmitting commands to it that lead to the movement of the processing tool beyond the permissible limits (i.e., commands prohibited for numerically controlled equipment).
This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to protect numerically controlled hardware from executing forbidden commands. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has privileges to transmit commands to numerically controlled equipment or the ability to change commands transmitted by a legitimate user.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of computer hardware and software reboots
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the user (violator) resetting the state of RAM (zeroing memory) by accidentally or intentionally rebooting individual devices, blocks, or the system as a whole. 
This threat is caused by the property of RAM to reset its state when shutting down and rebooting.
This threat can be implemented either in hardware (by pressing a button) or in software (locally or remotely) if the following conditions are met: 
the presence of open user sessions
in the system; the violator has rights in the system (or physical ability) to perform a forced reboot
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of integer variable overflow
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that an intruder can cause a discredited application to malfunction by feeding data of an unsupported format to its input interfaces or performing an operation using it, which will result in data of a format unsupported by the discredited application. 
This threat is caused by software vulnerabilities associated with insufficient verification of the correctness of input data by such applications, as well as the fact that operators of any software are able to correctly process only certain types of data (for example, only integers or only positive numbers).
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has: 
information about the range of input (or processed) data formats supported by the discredited application; 
the ability to interact with the input interface of the discredited application
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of interception of information entered and output to peripheral devices
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for an intruder to gain unauthorized access to information entered and output to peripheral devices by intercepting data processed by peripheral device controllers. 
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to protect information from leakage and control data flows, as well as the inability to protect information entered and output to peripheral devices using cryptographic means (since information should be presented to system users in an understandable form).
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder has privileges to install and run specialized malware that implements the functions of "keyloggers" (for obtaining user passwords by the intruder), virtual printer drivers (interception of documents containing protected information), etc.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of interception of data transmitted over a computer network
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access to the network traffic of the discredited computer network by an intruder in passive ("listening" to traffic) or active (packet substitution, changing their contents) mode to collect and analyze information (for example, authentication information), which can be used in the future to implement other threats, while remaining in the implementation of this threat. threats from an invisible (hidden) recipient of intercepted data. In addition, the intruder can conduct research on other types of data streams, such as radio signals.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network interaction mechanisms that provide third-party users with open data about the discredited system, as well as network software configuration errors. 
The implementation of this threat is possible under the following conditions:
 the intruder has access to a discredited computer network; 
the inability of the technologies used for data transmission to prevent the possibility of covert listening to the data stream
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of intercepting a privileged thread
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder's unauthorized access to the data stream created by an application with additional privileges (to a privileged data stream), by synchronous (calling a privileged function that returns an incorrect value) or asynchronous (creating callbacks, manipulating pointers, etc.) destructive software impact on it. 
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in software that uses sections of code executed with additional rights inherited by the created privileged threads (the presence of erroneous pointers, incorrect memory release, etc.). 
This threat can be implemented under the following conditions: 
in a discredited application, there are code sections that require execution with rights that exceed the rights of ordinary users; 
the intruder has privileges that allow you to make changes to the input data of the discredited application
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of intercepting a privileged process
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder obtaining control rights for a process that has high privileges (for example, inherited from a user or group of users who play the role of administrators of the discredited system) to execute arbitrary malicious code with the rights of the discredited process. 
This threat is caused by software vulnerabilities that perform access control functions (in the algorithm or configuration parameters), which lead to incorrect distribution of access rights within the tree of inherited processes.
This threat can be implemented if one of the following conditions is met: 
the intruder successfully enters incorrect data that leads to buffer overflow or certain types of software injections;
 the intruder has privileges to run system utilities intended for process management
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of hijacking of hypervisor control
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for an intruder to gain unauthorized access to information, software, and computing resources reserved and managed by the hypervisor by obtaining the right to manage the hypervisor by exploiting vulnerabilities in the hypervisor management console. 
This threat is caused by the hypervisor management console having software interfaces for interacting with other access subjects (processes, programs) and, as a result, the possibility of unauthorized access to this console (a virtualization-level program), as well as insufficient measures to differentiate access to this console.
This threat can be implemented if the violator has the rights to interact with the hypervisor management console
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Hypervisor, Hypervisor management console

column2: Threat of interception of management of the virtualization environment
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility for an intruder to gain unauthorized access to information, software, and computing resources reserved and managed by all hypervisors that implement the virtualization environment, by obtaining the right to manage these hypervisors by exploiting vulnerabilities in the console of the virtual infrastructure management tool.
This threat is caused by the console having a virtual infrastructure management tool implemented within one of the VMs, software interfaces for interacting with other access subjects (processes, programs), and, as a result, the possibility of unauthorized access to this console (a virtualization management level program), as well as insufficient measures to differentiate access to this console.
This threat can be implemented if the violator has the rights to interact with the virtual infrastructure management tool console
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of system registry corruption
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of breaking the availability of part of the functionality or the entire information system due to damage to the registry used in its operation due to incorrect shutdown of the operating system (uncontrolled reboot, errors in device drivers, etc.), violation of the integrity of files containing registry data, errors in the file system of the storage medium, or due to violator of destructive software impact on file objects containing the registry. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in access control measures for files containing registry data, backup and integrity control measures for such files, as well as measures to restore registry functionality due to operating system failures. 
The implementation of this threat is possible under one of the following conditions: 
errors occur in individual processes or the entire operating system;
 the violator has access rights to the registry or files containing registry data
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of privilege escalation
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator performing a destructive program influence on the discredited process (or system) or on other processes (or systems). on his (her) behalf by exploiting the violator's unlawfully obtained additional rights to manage the discredited object.
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the software that performs access control functions (in the algorithm or configuration parameters).
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has software (such as an "exploit") specifically designed to implement this threat in the discredited system.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: System software, Network software, information system

column2: BIOS Password Guessing threat
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access to the BIOS/UEFI settings by entering the BIOS/UEFI console using a password selected programmatically or "manually" using methods of total search of options or dictionary selection. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the authentication mechanism implemented in the BIOS/UEFI consoles. 
This threat can be implemented in one of the following cases: 
the intruder can have physical access to the computer and can restart it; 
the intruder has a special software tool for brute-forcing BIOS/UEFI passwords and privileges in the system to install and run such tools
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of tampering with event log entries
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder making changes to the security event logs of the discredited system (deleting records that compromise the intruder or falsifying records about events that did not occur) in order to mislead its administrators or hide traces of other threats. 
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to restrict access to the security event log. 
The implementation of this threat is possible in one of the following cases: 
security event logging technology assumes the ability to edit them and the intruder has the necessary privileges;
security event logging technology does not assume the ability to edit them, but the intruder has the necessary privileges to write to log files, as well as special software tools, capable of processing log files of the format used in the discredited system
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat to connect to a wireless network that bypasses the authentication procedure
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder intercepting wireless network traffic or other illegal actions by legalizing the intruder's own connection to the wireless network in semi-automatic mode (for example, WPS) without entering the encryption key. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the authentication procedure for wireless devices during semi-automatic connection.
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has physical access to a wireless access point that supports semi-automatic connection mode.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of spoofing a wireless client or access point
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder receiving authentication or other protected information transmitted during the automatic connection of wireless access points or client software to trusted network interaction subjects substituted by the intruder.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the authentication mechanism for network interaction subjects with wireless access.
This threat can be implemented if the intruder places a client or wireless access point with specially formed operation parameters (such as the MAC address, name, data transmission standard used, etc.) in the availability zone for discredited wireless access devices
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Network node, network software, hardware, wireless access point

column2: Threat of spoofing user actions by deception
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing illegal actions in the system on behalf of another user using social engineering methods (deceiving the user, imposing false beliefs) or technical methods (using transparent buttons, replacing labels on controls, etc.) 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the user interface or user errors.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the discredited user has the rights to perform the operations that the violator needs from him
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of spoofing a trusted user
column3:
The threat consists in the ability of an intruder to impersonate a legitimate user and receive / transmit data on their behalf. This threat can be described as "imitation of the client's actions".
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network communication technologies, which often do not allow you to authenticate the source / recipient of information. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has a computer network connection, as well as information about the configuration of network devices, the type of software used, and so on.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of spoofing a backup copy of the BIOS software
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the intruder indirectly introducing malicious code into the BIOS/UEFI of the discredited computer, by waiting or creating the need to perform the procedure for restoring the previous version of the BIOS/UEFI software, previously replaced by the intruder.
This threat is caused by insufficient access control and integrity control measures for BIOS/UEFI software backups. 
This threat can be implemented under the following conditions: 
the intruder has successfully replaced the backup copy of the BIOS/UEFI software; 
there is a need to restore the previous version of the BIOS/UEFI software (this condition can occur either accidentally or be provoked by the intruder)
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of spoofing the contents of network resources
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing unauthorized access to the protected data of network users or performing various fraudulent actions by covertly replacing the contents of data stored (sites, web pages) or transmitted (emails, network packets) over the network. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network communication technologies, which often do not allow you to authenticate the contents of an email message. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator has access rights to network resources and the network user does not have measures to ensure their integrity
column4: External intruder with low potential
column5: Application software, Network software, Network traffic

column2: Threat of spoofing the network access subject
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing unauthorized access to the protected data of network users or performing various fraudulent actions by covertly replacing information about the sender of the message in network requests sent by a discredited user. This threat can be described as "imitation of server actions". 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network communication technologies, which often do not allow you to authenticate the source of information. 
This threat can be implemented if the violator successfully impersonates the legitimate sender (for example, using false phishing websites). The key difference from the "threat of spoofing the content of network resources" is that in this case, the intruder does not change the original content of the electronic resource (website, email), but only official information.
column4: External intruder with medium potential
column5: Application software, Network software, Network traffic

column2: Threat of obtaining preliminary information about the security object
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator disclosing protected information about the security status of the discredited system, its configuration and potential vulnerabilities, etc., by taking measures to collect and analyze available information about the system. 
This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in network software that allow you to get information about the configuration of individual programs or the system as a whole (lack of input data control, open network ports, incorrect configuration of security policies, etc.). 
This threat can be implemented if information about the discredited system is obtained using at least one of the following methods for studying the discredited system: 
analysis of the system's responses to network requests (including syntactically incorrect or non-standard ones) to network services opened in the system, which can cause unhandled exceptions with detailed error messages containing protected information (stack trace, system configuration, network packet routing) 
analysis of system responses to string URI requests (including invalid SQL queries, alternative file access paths).
This threat differs from the threat of data interception and other data collection threats in that the intruder actively polls the discredited system, and does not just observe it
column4: External intruder with medium potential
column5: Network node, network software, network traffic, application software

column2: Threat of obtaining information about the owner of a wireless device
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator disclosing information about the geographical movements of the discredited user at certain time intervals, including revealing the place of his work, residence, etc. Obtaining such information can be used by the violator in the future to implement threats in information systems that the discredited user has access to. 
This threat is caused by the weak protection of the identification information of wireless access points when they are connected to the Internet.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has access to the identification data of stationary wireless access points, with which the discredited user's wireless device automatically interacts.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of loss of trust in a cloud service provider
column3:
The threat is the possibility of reducing the level of security and making additional errors in ensuring the security of information protected in the cloud system due to the irretrievable outflow of necessary resources from the cloud service provider due to the loss of trust in their provider by cloud service consumers. 
This threat is caused by the fact that due to the publication of facts about information security incidents related to a cloud service provider, there is a loss of trust in such a provider on the part of cloud service consumers, and, as a result, there is a need for an avalanche of resources (human, technical, financial) allocated by the cloud service provider to solve the problems that arise in this situation tasks (multiple user consultations, emergency revision of security policies, modernization of the security system, etc.), which can not only cause a lack of resources to ensure the current level of information security, but also provoke the admission of new errors "in a hurry". 
Implementation of this threat is possible in case of publication of single or multiple facts about information security incidents related to the cloud service provider, which caused significant losses for its customers.
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: File system objects, an information system migrated to the cloud

column2: Threat of loss and leakage of data processed in the cloud
column3:
The threat is the possibility of violating the confidentiality, integrity and availability of protected information of cloud service consumers processed in the cloud system. 
This threat is caused by weak security measures for information processed in the cloud system. 
This threat can be implemented if the provider (incorrect selection or configuration of security tools) or the consumer (loss of password, electronic key, login from an insecure console) of cloud services makes mistakes in ensuring the security of protected information
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: System software, metadata, and file system objects

column2: Threat of information loss due to inconsistency in the operation of big data storage nodes
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of making errors when copying protected information in distributed data storage on different nodes of the big data warehouse due to inconsistencies in their operation, which lead to the inability of a legal user to access blocks or all protected information. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the data replication mechanisms implemented in big data storage nodes. 
This threat can be implemented if one or several nodes are disabled or disabled due to special software actions on big data storage nodes, as well as technical or software failures in the operation of their components
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Information system, big data storage nodes

column2: Threat of loss of cloud resource management
column3:
The threat is the possibility of a breach of contractual obligations on the part of a cloud service provider in relation to their consumer due to the significant complexity of building an effective cloud resource management system for a cloud system, especially using the cloud resources of other cloud service providers. 
This threat is caused by the complexity of determining the logical and physical location of cloud resources, the lack of physical control measures for access to data warehouses, backups, etc. , as well as the need to take into account the specifics of information protection legislation in countries where cloud service providers are residents who perform the role of subcontractors for the provision of ordered cloud services. 
This threat can be implemented if meeting the requirements for the functionality of the cloud system becomes difficult (or impossible) due to the legal norms of other countries involved in cross-border transmission of cloud traffic
column4: External intruder with high potential

column2: Threat of losing control of your own infrastructure when moving it to the cloud
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of making mistakes in managing the infrastructure of a cloud service consumer's system that has been migrated to the cloud, on the part of the cloud service provider, because it does not have information about the management features of a particular system, as well as because the cloud service consumer who has such information does not have the ability to systems due to their immigration to the cloud.
This threat is caused by the inability of the cloud service consumer to reliably assess the real level of security provided by the cloud service provider in relation to the protected information of the cloud service consumer, due to the confidentiality of information about the technologies, software and technical solutions used by the cloud service provider, as well as specific settings for information security tools. 
This threat can be implemented if a part of the system management functions of the cloud service consumer is transferred to the cloud service provider (when migrating part or all of the system to the cloud).
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: Information system migrated to the cloud, system software, application software, network software

column2: The threat of overcoming physical defenses
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator performing almost any destructive actions against the discredited information system when they gain physical access to the computer hardware of the system by overcoming the physical access control system organized in the enterprise building.
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the physical access control system (lack of locks in the room, personnel errors, etc.). 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator successfully uses any of the methods of entering the object (deception of personnel, breaking locks, etc.).
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of bringing the system to a "denial of service"state
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of a discredited system refusing access to legitimate users in the event of an avalanche-like increase in the number of network connections to this system or when using shortcomings in the implementation of network protocols.
This threat is caused by the fact that the system consumes part of its resources to process each network request, as well as weaknesses in network technologies related to the limited speed of processing network request streams, insufficient control measures for connection management and errors in the implementation of network protocols.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the volume of requests exceeds the volume of resources available for processing them in the discredited system, or if there are errors in the implementation of network protocols (for example, generating an IP address of version 6 based on the MAC address, determining the availability of an IP address, using the PPP interface integrity control function, etc.).
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Information system, network node, system software, network software, network traffic, telecommunication device

column2: Threat of linking to a cloud service provider
column3:
The threat is the possibility of difficult (or even unsolvable) problems of a technical, organizational, legal, or other nature that prevent the consumer of cloud services from changing their provider.
This threat is caused by the lack of compatibility between data formats and software interfaces used in cloud infrastructures of various cloud service providers. 
This threat can be implemented if the cloud service provider uses non-standard software or virtual machine image format, and there are no tools to convert the virtual machine image from the format it uses to another one (used by another provider).
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: Information system migrated to the cloud, system software, network software, network traffic, file system objects

column2: Threat of suspension of cloud services due to technical failures
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of reducing the quality of cloud services (or even refusing to provide them to end users) due to technical failures of at least one of the cloud service providers (part of the chain of intermediaries in providing cloud services to their end users), as well as due to significant delays or losses in data transmission channels rented by the consumer or cloud service providers. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the procedure for monitoring the performance of maintenance and compliance with the operating modes of technical means of the cloud information system. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if there are no backup mechanisms for processing, storing and transmitting information that are part of the cloud information system.

column2: Threat of software failure of information storage, processing, and/or input/output / transmission facilities
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder interrupting the technology of information processing in a discredited system by performing destructive software (locally or remotely) effects on storage facilities (external, removable and internal drives), processing (processor, device controller, etc.) and (or) input/output/transmission of information (keyboards, etc.), in particular:  as a result, the security object will go to the "denial of service" state. However, it may not be possible to recover it from this state by restarting the system, but it will require repair and restoration work. 
This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in the firmware of information storage, processing, and (or) input/output/transmission facilities, as well as the inability to store, process, and (or) input/output/transmission facilities for a long time in the mode of maximum permissible values (frequency of the system bus, central processor, number of read accesses, etc.).or record and other parameters).
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator has the rights to send a command or specially generated input data to the storage, processing, and (or) input/output/transmission of information.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Information carrier, firmware, hardware, telecommunication device

column2: Threat of software reset of the BIOS password
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access to the BIOS/UEFI settings by entering an "empty" password after restarting the computer.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the operating system's access control measures for the BIOS/UEFI password reset function. 
The implementation of this threat is possible under the following conditions:
 if the BIOS/UEFI software has an active interface for programmatically resetting the password directly from under the operating system;
 if the intruder has special software tools that implement password reset, as well as rights in the operating system to install and run these tools
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of missing software integrity checks
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder introducing malicious software into a discredited system by fraudulently redirecting requests from the user or its programs to its own network resource containing malicious software, for its "manual" or" automatic " download and subsequent installation in the discredited system on behalf of the user or its programs. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanisms for verifying the integrity of software files and/or verifying the authenticity of the source of their receipt. 
This threat can be implemented if deceptive techniques are successfully used using one of the following methods: 
"manual method" – the intruder, using deceptive mechanisms, persuades the user to follow a link to the intruder's network resource, which leads to the launch of malicious code on the user's computer, or convinces the user to download and install malicious software on their own (for example, under the guise of a game or antivirus tool); 
"automatic method" – the intruder performs a destructive effect by redirecting the automatic update function of the discredited program to its own malicious server
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: System software, Application software, Network software

column2: Threat of direct access to the memory of the computing field of a supercomputer
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder's process operating in the computing field of a supercomputer reading protected data from RAM allocated for a parallel (discredited) process using remote direct memory access operations. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the direct RAM access protocol, which is used to access a memory segment allocated for a remote parallel process operating in the computing field of a supercomputer. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder successfully accesses the input/output data of parallel processes in the computing field of the supercomputer
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Computing nodes of a supercomputer, data transmission channels of a supercomputer, system software

column2: Threat of unauthorized extension of elevated rights to the entire grid system
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of automatic distribution to the entire grid system of unauthorized privileges obtained by an intruder on a single node. 
This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in the client software of the grid system and weaknesses in the mechanism for assigning rights to users implemented in the binding software. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator successfully increases his rights on one node of the grid system.
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: Grid system resource centers, grid system nodes, grid system, network software

column2: Threat of failure of automatic management of the big data storage access control system
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of situations related to errors in automatically assigning access rights to users (granting additional permissions, erroneous inheritance, accidental restoration of "inactive" accounts, etc.). 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the control measures for a large number (from a thousand, and in some cases up to several million) of user accounts by security administrators. 
This threat can be implemented if there are failures or errors in the operation of the big data storage access control system
column5: Information system, big data storage access control system

column2: Threat of failure in processing specially modified files
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator performing various illegal actions on behalf of discredited applications by causing a malfunction in their operation by making changes to the files processed by discredited programs or their metadata. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the mechanism for checking the integrity of processed files and the correctness of the data contained in them. 
This threat can be implemented
if:  the intruder has information about the file formats and values that cause discredited applications to fail when processing them;  a
mechanism that has been successfully created in the discredited system to intercept control over the violator's processing of a program failure
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Metadata, file system objects, and system software

column2: Threat of failure of the BIOS update process
column3:
The threat is the possibility of disabling the computer due to the introduction of critical errors in the BIOS/UEFI software as a result of a violation of the update process. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the BIOS/UEFI software update monitoring technologies. 
This threat can be implemented during computer repair and maintenance, both when installing a correct / compatible update version (due to crashes, interference, etc.), and when installing a damaged / incompatible update version (due to the lack of an integrity and compatibility check mechanism).
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: BIOS/UEFI firmware and hardware, communication channels

column2: Threat of scanning web services developed based on the WSDL description language
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder obtaining information about the current configuration of web services and the presence of vulnerabilities in it by examining the WSDL interface of the web server. 
This threat is caused by insufficient information privacy measures implemented in WSDL services that provide detailed information about ports, services, and connections available to users. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has network access to the network resource under investigation and special software tools for scanning the network
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of deleting authentication information
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of denying legitimate users access to information resources, as well as in the possibility of an intruder obtaining the privileges of a discredited user by resetting (zeroing, deleting) his authentication information. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the policy of restricting access to authentication information and tools for working with user accounts.
This threat can be implemented if one of the following conditions is met: 
regular tools for working with user accounts have the functionality of resetting authentication information, and the violator has received privileges in the discredited system to use these tools; 
the violator has special software that implements the function of resetting authentication information, and has received privileges in the discredited system to use these tools
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of increased impact on users ' computing resources using third-party servers
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Information system, network node, system software, network software

column2: Threat of installing vulnerable versions of the BIOS software update
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of introducing vulnerabilities in the BIOS/UEFI software during its update, which can be used later to bring the computer into a "denial of service" state, unauthorized changes to the BIOS/UEFI configuration, or execution of malicious code every time the computer starts up. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to control the absence of vulnerabilities in the newly released versions of the BIOS/UEFI software update. 
The implementation of this threat is possible during the repair and maintenance of the computer
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of loss of computing resources
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Information system, network node, storage medium, system software, network software, network traffic

column2: Threat of loss of data carriers
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of disclosure of information stored on a lost medium (if there is no data encryption), or its loss (if there is no data backup).
This threat is caused by weaknesses in data storage registration and accounting measures, as well as backup measures for protected data.
The implementation of this threat is possible due to employee negligence
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of physical failure of information storage, processing, and/or input/output / transmission facilities
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an external intruder intentionally disabling the means of storing, processing, and / or I / O / transmitting information, which may lead to a violation of the availability, and in some cases, the integrity of the protected information. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in physical access control measures for storing, processing, and/or I/O / transmitting information. 
Implementation of this threat is possible if the violator obtains physical access to information storage media (external, removable, and internal drives), information processing facilities (processor, device controllers, etc.), and information input/output facilities (keyboard, etc.).
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Media formatting threat
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: The threat of "forced web browsing"
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder gaining access to protected information, performing privileged operations, or performing other destructive actions on incorrectly protected components of web applications. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses (or lack of) of the mechanism for checking the correctness of entered data on web servers. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if you successfully "manually enter" certain addresses of web pages in the address bar of the web browser and forcibly navigate through the website tree to pages that are not explicitly linked on the website
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of theft of information storage, processing, and/or input/output / transmission facilities
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an external intruder stealing a computer (and its connected devices), USB drives, optical disks, or other means of storing, processing, I/O, or transmitting information. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in physical access control measures for storing, processing, and/or I/O / transmitting information. 
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has physical access to information storage media (external, removable, and internal drives), information processing facilities (processor, device controllers, etc.), and information input/output facilities (keyboard, etc.).
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of excessive use of computing resources of the supercomputer during intensive interprocessor message exchange
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of a "denial of service" situation on the part of the computing field of the supercomputer. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to control the distribution of computing resources of the supercomputer when processing a task with multiple processors. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the supercomputer performs specific computational tasks, during which interprocessor messages are generated with high intensity
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of exploiting the digital signature of program code
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of catching an exception / signal from a privileged function block
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of denial-of-service status propagation in cloud infrastructure
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of spreading negative consequences from the implementation of threats at the physical or virtual level of the cloud infrastructure to the management and orchestration levels, as well as to all information systems deployed on the basis of discredited cloud infrastructure. 
This threat is caused by the inability of information systems to function in the cloud if the cloud infrastructure itself does not work correctly, as well as the dependence of the health of the upper levels of the cloud infrastructure on the health of the lower ones. 
This threat can be implemented if the cloud infrastructure at the physical or virtual level of the cloud infrastructure is put in a denial-of-service state
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Cloud infrastructure created using virtualization technologies

column2: Threat of inclusion of components that are not reliably tested in the project
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of violating the security of protected information due to the choice of components for use in the system that are not in accordance with their functional characteristics, reliability, availability of certificates, etc. specified by the designer. 
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to control errors during the design of security-related systems. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if you choose to use components in the system at a price, advertised, etc.
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: Software, technical means, information system, key system of information infrastructure

column2: Threat of introducing system redundancy
column3:
The threat is the possibility of reducing the speed of data processing (i.e. availability) by software components (or the system as a whole) due to the introduction of redundant components (initially unnecessary or unnecessary when making changes to the project).
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to control errors during the design of security-related systems. 
Implementation of this threat is possible if changes are made to the list of tasks solved by the designed software (designed system).
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: Software, information system, key information infrastructure system

column2: Threat of computer infection when visiting unreliable sites
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of violating the security of protected information by malicious programs that are secretly installed when system users visit sites with unreliable content from their workplaces (intentionally or accidentally redirected) and run with the privileges of discredited users.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network traffic filtering and anti-virus control mechanisms at the organization level. 
This threat can be implemented if users of the system visit sites with unreliable content from their workplaces
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of "theft" of the network service access account
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized familiarization by the violator with the protected user information by obtaining identification/authentication information corresponding to the user's access account to network services (social network, cloud services, etc.), which is associated with an inactive/non-existent email address.
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to control the activity/existence of email mailboxes.
This threat can be implemented under the following conditions:
 if the email address associated with the user's access account to network services has the "free to borrow" status (for example, if the user specified a non-existent address during registration or did not access the mailbox for a long time, as a result of which it was disabled);
 if the intruder has information about about the email address associated with the discredited user's account for accessing network services
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of developer mechanisms
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of intercepting program management through the use of debugging mechanisms (special software functions or hardware elements that help you test and debug tools during their development).
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to control errors during the development of information security tools. 
This threat can be implemented if debugging mechanisms are not removed in the program.
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized encryption of information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of actual loss of availability of protected data due to their unauthorized cryptographic transformation by an intruder using a secret key known only to him.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in antivirus protection, as well as in access control mechanisms. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the intruder successfully installs a cryptographic information conversion tool on the discredited computer, as well as successfully detects (identifies) the protected files by the intruder
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of covert inclusion of a computing device in the botnet
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the intruder's indirect destructive impact on information systems from a variety of computing devices (computers, mobile technical equipment, etc.) connected to the Internet, by seizing control of such devices by unauthorized installation of:
malicious software of the Backdoor type to provide the intruder with the ability to remotely access/control the discredited computing device;
client software for inclusion in the botnet and use of the botnet created in this way for various illegal purposes (sending spam, conducting denial-of-service attacks, etc.). 
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the network software and weaknesses in the anti-virus control and firewall mechanisms. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if there is an exit from the discredited computing device to the Internet
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: The threat of the spread of "mail worms"
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of violating the security of the user's protected information by malicious programs that are secretly installed when system users receive emails containing malicious software such as "mail worm", as well as unwittingly participating in further illegal distribution of malicious code.
This threat is caused by weaknesses in the anti-virus control mechanisms.
This threat can be implemented if the discredited user has an electronic mailbox, as well as at least one address of another user in their address book.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Web Server Spam Threat
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of illegal mass distribution of commercial, political, fraudulent and other messages to the web server by the violator without a request from the discredited web servers. 
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the mechanisms for filtering messages coming from the Internet.
This threat can be implemented if the discredited web server has activated functionality that implements various mail servers, instant message delivery services, blogs, forums, web store auctions, online SMS messaging services, online voting services, etc.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: The threat of "pharming"
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized familiarization by the violator with the protected information (including identification/authentication) of the user by secretly redirecting the user to a fake site (which looks the same as the original one), where the discredited user is required to enter the protected information. 
This threat is caused by vulnerabilities in the DNS server and router.
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has: 
information about specific sites visited by the user that require entering protected information; 
tools for creating and launching a fake site; 
special software tools of the "exploit" type that redirect the user to a fake site. 
In addition, this type of threat affects genuine sites that do not require establishing a secure connection before entering restricted access information.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Phishing threat
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized familiarization by the violator with the protected information (including identification/authentication) of the user by convincing him using social engineering methods (including sending targeted emails (the so-called spear-phishing attack), using calls with a question about opening an email attachment, imitation of advertising offers (fake offers) or various applications (fake apps)) go to a fake site (which looks the same as the original one), where the discredited user is required to enter protected information or open an infected attachment in an email. 
This threat is caused by insufficient knowledge of users about the methods and means of "phishing".
This threat can be implemented if the intruder has: 
information about specific sites visited by the user that require entering protected information; 
tools for creating and launching a fake site; 
information about the user's contacts with a trusted organization (phone number, email address, etc.). 
Fake emails from the administration of an organization that the user interacts with (for example, a bank)are most often used to persuade the user to disclose restricted access information (or open an attachment to an email)
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Risk of disruption of the technological / production process due to time delays introduced by the security tool
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of bringing the system into a "denial of service" state or disrupting the normal functioning mode due to a time delay in real-time systems introduced into the processes of transmitting and processing protected information by information security tools, caused by the need to process the transmitted / processed information in order to identify and neutralize information security threats. 
The implementation of this threat is affected not only by the range of information security tools used, their settings, the amount of information transmitted/processed, but also by the current activity of external intruders whose software impacts are processed by information security tools.
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unconfirmed data entry by the operator into a security-related system
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of errors in the system operation due to the absence (or ignoring) of a procedure for detecting and correcting errors in the data entered during operation by the operator himself, before activating the managed equipment. In addition, the implementation of this threat may result in incorrectly implemented (or missing) means of responding to incorrect, spontaneous actions of the operator, tools for taking into account the lower/upper limits of the speed and direction of the operator's reaction, response schemes for double-tapping keys when entering normal and critical data, procedures for forming time pauses with the ability to choose different answers (yes/no, etc.). 
The feasibility of this threat depends on the requirements for detecting and correcting errors in the data entered into the security-related system, as well as the difference between these requirements and the actual level of error detection and correction.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder
column5: System software, Network software, Application software, Hardware

column2: Threat of unauthorized use of system and network utilities
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder performing a destructive software impact on the system through the use of existing or pre-implemented standard (known and usually undetected by antivirus programs as malicious) system and network utilities intended for use by the administrator for diagnostics and maintenance of the system (network).
The implementation of this threat is possible under the following conditions: 
the presence of standard system and network utilities in the system or their successful implementation by the intruder into the system and hiding (using existing archives, "hidden" or "read-only" attributes, etc.);
 the intruder has privileges to run such utilities
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized modification of protected information
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of violating the integrity of the protected information by performing a destructive physical impact on the machine storage medium or destructive software impact (including changing individual bits or completely erasing information) on the data stored on it. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator obtains system rights to write data or physical access to the machine storage medium at a distance sufficient to provide an effective destructive impact.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of failure of the temperature control subsystem
column3:
The threat is the possibility of damage to part of the system components or the system as a whole due to the temperature regime of their operation exceeding the specified requirements due to the failure of the ventilation subsystems and temperature devices included in it. 
The implementation of this threat is possible both due to natural man-made causes, and by carrying out certain measures by the violator aimed at remotely disabling / disabling components of the temperature control subsystem.
column4: Internal intruder with low potential; External intruder with medium potential
column5: Technical means of air conditioning, including pipeline systems for cooling air circulation in the data center, programmable logic controllers, distributed control systems, management systems, and other software control tools

column2: Threat of real-time interception of one-time passwords
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder taking control of critical user operations by intercepting one-time passwords sent by the system automatically and using them to perform illegal actions before their validity period expires (usually no more than 5 minutes).
This threat can be implemented if the following conditions
are met: the intruder has information about the identification/authentication information of the discredited user of a conditional permanent action; 
the intruder successfully intercepts traffic between the system and the user
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of physical obsolescence of hardware components
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of disruption of the system's security-related functionality due to failures of hardware components of this system due to their physical obsolescence (rust, rapid wear, oxidation, contamination, peeling, peeling, etc.) due to the influence of the physical environment (humidity, dust, corrosive substances).
The possibility of implementing this threat increases when users use technical means in conditions that do not meet the requirements set by their manufacturer.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of control interception by an automated process control system
column4: External intruder with high potential; Internal intruder with medium potential
column5: Software of the automated process control system

column2: Threat of data aggregation processed using a mobile device
