column2: Threat of unauthorized modification of information security settings
column3: The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder making unauthorized changes to the settings of the information security tool. This threat is caused by weaknesses in measures to restrict access to configuration files of the information security tool. The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator obtains access rights to the software management interface of the information security tool, as well as if the violator has information about the structure and format of the configuration files of the information security tool.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of malicious code injection through ads, services, and content
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder introducing malicious code into the information system through advertising, services and (or) content (i.e. convincing the system user to activate the link, code, etc.) when the system user visits sites on the Internet or installs programs with the function of displaying ads. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in network traffic filtering and anti-virus control mechanisms at the organization level. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if users of the system visit sites on the Internet from their workplaces
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of unauthorized impact on the information security tool
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access by the violator to the software environment for managing the information security tool and changing the mode of its operation. 
The threat is caused by the availability of a software management environment and interaction with system users for information protection tools. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if the violator obtains access rights to the software interface for managing the information security tool
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of software spoofing
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder introducing malicious software into the system by downloading and installing malicious software hidden under the guise of legitimate freely distributed software. 
This threat is caused by the user's rights to install software from the Internet.
The implementation of this threat is possible when downloading software on the Internet
column4: An internal intruder with an average potential
column5: Application software, Network software, System software

column2: Threat of masking malicious code actions
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of hiding malicious code actions in the system due to the use of special code masking mechanisms (archiving, changing the data format, etc.), which prevent its further analysis. 
This threat is caused by the presence of methods for masking program code that are not taken into account by the signature databases of information security tools, as well as operating system mechanisms that allow you to search for information security modules. 
This threat can be implemented if the system uses outdated versions of information protection tools
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of introducing malicious code by visiting infected sites on the Internet
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of malicious code being introduced into the software distribution
column3: The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder infecting the system by installing an untrusted distribution kit with malicious code embedded in it. This threat is caused by weaknesses in anti-virus protection measures. This threat can be implemented if: the user uses third-party distributions; there is no antivirus check before installing the distribution.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Application software, Network software, System software

column2: Threat of using vulnerable software versions
column3: The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder having a destructive impact on the system by exploiting software vulnerabilities. This threat is caused by weaknesses in the software's vulnerability analysis mechanisms. The implementation of this threat is possible if you do not check for vulnerabilities before using the software, or if you use software that has been discontinued by the manufacturer
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential
column5: Application software, Network software, System software

column2: Threat of information leakage due to the use of malicious software traffic encryption algorithms
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of information leakage due to the use of malicious software traffic encryption algorithms that hide the very fact of data transfer. 
This threat is caused by weaknesses in information security measures for storing, processing, and transmitting information resources. 
This threat can be implemented: 
if the specified malicious software is successfully introduced into the discredited system; 
if there is no or insufficient implementation of firewall measures
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized use of privileged functions of a mobile device
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility that the violator can remove the manufacturer's pre-installed restrictions on configuring privileged functions of the mobile device. This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in the operating systems of the mobile device that allow access to the settings of privileged functions. 
This threat can be implemented if an intruder gains access to a mobile device
column4: External intruder with high potential

column2: Threat of remote execution of malicious code bypassing the operating system's security mechanisms
column4: External intruder with high potential
column5: Fixed and mobile devices (computers and laptops) (hardware device)

column2: Threat of malware controlling the list of apps running on a mobile device
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of using malware to control the list of applications running on a mobile device. 
This threat is caused by insufficient anti-virus protection measures, which allows you to perform uncontrolled launch of malicious programs (lack of control of authorized software). This threat can be implemented if the malware is embedded on a mobile device and unintentionally launched by the user
column4: External intruder with high potential

column2: Threat of theft of authentication information from temporary cookies
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility that malicious software can steal users ' authentication information and their accounts stored in temporary cookies, and transmit this information to intruders via the open RDP port. 
This threat is caused by insufficient anti-virus protection measures, which allows you to perform uncontrolled launch of malicious software (lack of control of authorized software).
In addition, this threat is caused by the failure to take measures to erase residual information from temporary files (clearing temporary files).
This threat can be implemented if the RDP port is open on the attacked computer.
column4: External intruder with medium potential
column5: Information stored on your computer in temporary files (software)

column2: Threat of hidden registration of administrator accounts by malicious software
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of the embedded malware secretly creating accounts with administrator rights in order to use them later for unauthorized access to user information and software settings installed on the infected computer. 
This threat is caused by insufficient anti-virus protection measures, which allows you to perform uncontrolled launch of malicious software (lack of control over the allowed software).
In addition, this threat is caused by insufficient measures to differentiate access (control the creation of user accounts).
This threat can be implemented if the RDP port is open on the attacked computer.
column4: External intruder with medium potential
column5: Access control system built into the computer's operating system (software)

column2: Threat of interception of mobile device control when using virtual voice assistants
column3:
The threat lies in the ability to control the mobile device and applications running on it on behalf of a legitimate user by transmitting these commands via virtual voice assistants (for example, via Siri for iPhone).
This threat is caused by problems with user authentication, in particular by Voice ID. The voice assistant cannot be completely sure that the voice being addressed belongs to the owner of the device, so for the convenience of users and to guarantee operation, the Voice ID sensitivity is set to low. This allows the intruder to use the speech recorded on the voice recorder of the owner of the mobile device. This threat can be implemented if the virtual voice assistant is in the active state (i.e., not disabled) and the voice ID sensitivity is set to low
column4: External intruder with medium potential
column5: Mobile device and applications running on it (software, hardware device)

column2: Threat of information theft from a mobile device when using virtual voice assistants
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of theft of user data from their mobile device through virtual voice assistants (for example, via Siri for iPhone).
This threat is caused by problems with user authentication, in particular by Voice ID. The voice assistant cannot be completely sure that the voice that is being accessed belongs to the owner of the device, so for the convenience of users and to guarantee operation, the Voice ID sensitivity is set to low. This allows the intruder to use the speech recorded on the voice recorder of the owner of the mobile device. This threat can be implemented if the virtual voice assistant is in the active state (i.e. not disabled) and the voice ID sensitivity is set to low
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of user data leakage when using the automatic filling in of authentication information in the browser
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of user data leakage due to the use of the automatic filling in authorization forms function implemented in browsers. 
The implementation of this threat is caused by storing user data used for autofilling authorization forms in clear text in browsers. 
This threat can be implemented if the user uses a browser that implements and activates the function of automatic filling in authorization forms.
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized installation of apps on mobile devices
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of installing applications on virtual machines of mobile devices running the Android operating system, which were launched without authorization by an embedded malicious program. The malicious program starts a virtual machine on a mobile device and hosts (installs) an unlimited number of applications in this virtual machine. 
This threat is caused by insufficient measures to control the launch of application software, which allows you to perform uncontrolled launch of malicious application software after the user performs various actions in the system (for example, when the user tries to close unwanted ads).
This threat can be implemented if there is a malicious program on the mobile device that can launch a VM and install an application in this VM.
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of information leakage from computers that are not connected to the Internet
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of data theft from computers that are not connected to the Internet by compromising their hardware elements or switching equipment devices (for example, routers) equipped with LED indicators, fixing the flickering of these indicators and decrypting the results obtained. 
The implementation of this threat is due to the fact that there is a possibility of unauthorized access to control these indicators (using special firmware or privilege escalation and executing malicious code), which allows transmitting information by converting it into a sequence of indicator signals for computers and switching equipment. 
The implementation of this threat is possible provided that the attacker has obtained physical access to the compromised computer or switching equipment to install a means of visual removal of LED indicator signals.
column4: External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized modification of parameter values of programmable logic controllers by malicious software
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized modification of the values of parameters for monitoring and controlling executive devices in programmable logic controllers by a malicious program after its penetration and authorization on these devices. 
The implementation of the threat is caused by the ability of a malicious program to detect programmable logic controllers on the network, to penetrate and function in the operating system of programmable logic controllers, as well as by shortcomings in authentication mechanisms. 
Implementation of this threat is possible provided that there is a possibility of access to the elements of the automated process control system via the Internet
column4: External intruder with medium potential

column2: Threat of computer malfunction and blocking access to its data due to incorrect operation of the security tools installed on it
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of disrupting the operation of the computer and denying access to its data due to the erroneous blocking of files by the information protection tool.
The implementation of this threat is due to the fact that the computer has an information protection tool that implements the function of blocking files
column4: External intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of equipment failure due to changes in its geolocation information
column3: The threat consists in the failure of the CNC equipment caused by a change in the geolocation information about this equipment. The threat is caused by the geolocation binding of CNC equipment to a specific geographical coordinate during commissioning. The threat is realized if the CNC equipment is moved and leads to the impossibility of its further operation
column4: External intruder with high potential

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to hardware configuration parameters through the use of "master codes "(engineering passwords)
column3: The threat consists in unauthorized access to information configuration parameters in CNC equipment through the use of special " master codes "(engineering passwords)," hardcoded " (not changed by configuration) in the software of this equipment. The threat is caused by the need for repair work in case of failures in the software of CNC equipment by representatives of the manufacturer
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of misuse of computing resources of computer equipment
column3:
The threat lies in the possibility of using the computing resources of computer equipment for implementing third-party computing processes.
The threat is implemented through the introduction of a malicious program containing code that implements the use of computing resources for its own needs (in particular, for cryptocurrency mining).
This threat is caused by insufficient information security measures: 
measures for anti-virus protection, which allows you to install and run a malicious program; 
measures to restrict the software environment, which allow the intruder to launch software components without control.
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential; External intruder with medium potential; Internal intruder with medium potential

processor cores
column4: External intruder with low potential; Internal intruder with low potential

column2: Threat of disruption of the information system caused by updating the software used in it
column3:
The threat is a possible disruption of the functioning of software, hardware and software elements of the information system or the information system as a whole due to incorrect operation of installed updates (patches) of the system software. 
The threat is caused by the presence of critical errors, defects, and vulnerabilities in the information system software used. 
The implementation of this threat is possible if updates are installed on the hardware and software components of the information system.
column4: A high-potential domestic intruder
column5: Hardware device, firmware, system and application software

column2: Threat of using unverified user data when generating a configuration file used by information systems administration software
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of a destructive impact on the information system and the information processed by it as a result of the operation of the software used for the administration of information systems.
This threat is related to weaknesses in the procedure for verifying user data used when generating a configuration file for information systems administration software.
The implementation of this threat is possible if the information system uses information systems administration software, which uses configuration files generated on the basis of user data as source data.
column4: Low-potential domestic intruder

column2: Threat of information system management interception
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of unauthorized access to information, software, and computing resources of an information system by an intruder as a result of substitution of centralized management tools for the information system or its components. 
This threat is caused by the presence of software interfaces for interaction with other access subjects (processes, programs) in centralized management tools and, as a result, the possibility of unauthorized access to these centralized management tools, as well as insufficient measures to differentiate access to them.

column2: Threat of bypassing multi-factor authentication
column3:
The threat consists in the ability to bypass multi-factor authentication by injecting malicious code into the discredited system and components involved in the multi-factor authentication procedure. 
This threat is caused
by:  software vulnerabilities; 
weaknesses in anti-virus protection and access control measures. 
This threat can be implemented:
if the discredited user works with files coming from untrusted sources; 
if they have software installation privileges

column2: Threat of late detection and response by components of an information (automated) system (including information security tools) to information security events
column3:
The threat consists in the omission and / or significant time delay in determining (detecting) information security events, which leads to a lack of response to attempts of unauthorized access to the information (automated) system, to the introduction of malicious programs. 
This threat is caused by incorrect configuration of components of the information (automated) system and/or information security tools, as well as the absence of such components and/or information security tools. 
This threat can be implemented if there are no security measures related to monitoring, collecting and analyzing data on information security events (no security event registration measures).

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to the system using third-party services
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of the violator performing destructive software influence on the discredited system using third-party legitimate services (social networks, instant messengers, code repositories, etc.) used as an intermediary. 
This threat can be implemented if the discredited system is already compromised.

column2: Threat of unauthorized access to applications installed on Smart cards
column3:
The threat consists in the possibility of an intruder's unauthorized access to applications installed on Smart cards by sending specially generated control commands (for example, specially generated SMS messages sent to the SIM card).
This threat is caused by the presence of vulnerabilities in applications installed on Smart cards.
Implementation of this threat is possible when using Smart cards of the Java Card type
